resources.string: Play modes, skip silence, known words, AnkiDroid, blur box
Pauses when each subtitle line ends. Press play for the next line.
Stops at the start of each line so you can read it before you hear it.
Hides subtitles while the video plays, then pauses after each line and shows them.
Plays each line several times before going on.
Pause on lines with one new word
Pauses only after lines with exactly one word you do not know yet. Needs Known words.
Turn on Known words below to use this mode.
Play modes and skip silence work when the full transcript is loaded, not with live subtitles.
Parts with no subtitle line for more than 1.5 seconds play faster or are skipped. Your own speed comes back before the next line.

Shows how much of each video you already know. Automatic also counts a word as known once you have seen it in enough lines (each line counts once per video; saved words are not counted). Manual uses only \"I know this word\" on the word card.
Gives words that are neither known nor saved a light background.
Every word you marked as known, in every language, is forgotten. Saved words stay.

Shows Send to AnkiDroid on the word card and in Practice → Export when AnkiDroid is installed. Cards go to a DualSub Replay deck. Keep AnkiDroid open in the background: on many phones it only accepts cards while it is running.
Puts a blurred box on the video to hide subtitles burned into the picture. Drag it to move it, and drag its corner to resize it.
Load captions with a page token (beta)
Automatic asks with a token only when YouTube sends empty captions, then asks with one first on the next videos while that keeps working. On always asks with a token first. Off never makes one.
You know %1$d%% of the words in this video.
Mark all new words as known
AnkiDroid is not installed on this phone.
AnkiDroid\'s permission was not given, so no card was added.
AnkiDroid did not accept the card. Open AnkiDroid, leave it running in the background, then come back and try again.
Every word was already sent to AnkiDroid.

resources.string: Count a word as known after seeing it
The subtitle panel then shows how much of each video you already know, and words you see often count as known by themselves. You can change this later in Settings → Study tools.
